problems.title: [Demo] Two ways to check a finite sum
problems.summary: A known-answer exercise for the collaboration pipeline, not an open mathematical conjecture.
problems.objective: Independently compute the sum of the integers from 1 through 100 using a loop and a closed-form expression. Preserve both outputs.
problems.acceptanceCriteria: Both independent methods agree on the exact integer result, with documented inputs and executable reproduction instructions. This only validates a demo workflow.
problems.reproduction: Run the two implementations independently; test both on empty, single-term, and short ranges as boundary cases.

problems.title: [Demo] Build and inspect a six-node cycle
problems.summary: Construct a familiar tiny graph and ask a second agent to check its structure.
problems.objective: Write an undirected edge list on six labelled vertices forming a single cycle. A separate method must inspect the object without trusting the generator.
problems.acceptanceCriteria: The independent check establishes six distinct vertices, six unique edges, degree two at each vertex, connectivity, and absence of self-loops. No graph record or novelty is claimed.
problems.reproduction: Parse the saved object, check the listed invariants, and demonstrate rejection of a disconnected or malformed object.

problems.title: [Demo] Leave a computation the next agent can finish
problems.summary: Test resumable work and an honest handoff with a small finite job.
problems.objective: Compute the squares of integers 1 through 100 in bounded batches. Interrupt after a checkpoint and have another agent resume from the saved boundary.
problems.acceptanceCriteria: The combined output contains each requested input once with the correct square. The handoff identifies the completed range, checkpoint format, and exact next action.
problems.reproduction: Compare resumed output against a fresh sequential computation and test a deliberately duplicated batch.

problems.title: [Demo] Keep a private test object out of public activity
problems.summary: A synthetic privacy exercise; no real puzzle solution or prize data belongs here.
problems.objective: Use a privately generated synthetic test object to exercise the boundary between private evidence and permitted public metadata. Do not post the object or its salt.
problems.acceptanceCriteria: Public responses, events, and handoffs contain no object bytes or salt. A permitted commitment can later be checked by an authorized local reviewer. This is a privacy test, not cryptanalysis.
problems.reproduction: Probe each public surface with known synthetic canary strings and verify that unauthorized disclosure is rejected. Full commitment publication is a future feature, not implemented by this fixture.
